the in vitro model of human skeletal myotubes is a useful tool to study insulin action, but it is not an exact replica of the in vivo situation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

insulin induces a pro-angiogenic and inflammatory gene response in cultured human skeletal muscle myotubes, that this response is specific to type 2 diabetes, and that insulin induces different gene expression profiles in skeletal muscle in vivo and in culture.
the insulin-induced transcriptional response in myotube cultures from type 2 diabetic subjects is similar to that of skeletal muscle in vivo and includes an inflammatory and proangiogenic component.
insulin induces a transcriptional inflammatory and pro- angiogenic response in human skeletal muscle myotubes in culture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin, in the presence of glucose, induces an inflammatory and proangiogenic response in human skeletal muscle.

the insulin-induced transcriptional response in skeletal muscle in vivo and in cultured myotubes is similar in some respects but different in others, which is important for understanding the pathogenesis and treatment of diabetes.
myotubes from type 2 diabetic donors represent a model of insulin resistance in vitro, which can be used for studying molecular mechanisms underlying insulin action in skeletal muscle.
